extracted.intended_audience: Federal agencies (OPM, Secretaries of State/Interior/Veterans Affairs), agency heads, uniformed service leadership, and federal employees affected by pay schedules
extracted.subtask_description: An Executive Order that sets federal pay rates and allowances by attaching schedules and prescribes regulatory responsibilities for applying interim geographic adjustments. It directs specific agencies to issue implementing regulations and identifies effective dates and superseded orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority for order
rubrics_metrics.description: By the authority vested in the President by the Constitution and specified statutes (including various sections of Public Laws and titles in the U.S. Code), the adjustments are ordered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists statutory bases (e.g., section 704 of Public Law 101–194; section 302 of the Federal Employees Pay Comparability Act of 1990; sections of titles 2, 3, 5, 22, 28, etc.) establishing legal authority for the order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory pay systems — rates set by attached schedules
rubrics_metrics.description: The rates of basic pay or salaries of the statutory pay systems (as defined in 5 U.S.C. 5302(1)) are set forth on the schedules attached hereto and made a part hereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically identifies the schedules attached to the order as the authoritative source for pay rates; agencies and employees must refer to the attached schedules for exact rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Schedule rates (Schedule 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The General Schedule (5 U.S.C. 5332(a)) pay rates are set forth at Schedule 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedule 1 attached to the Executive Order contains the specific step/grade rates for General Schedule employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign Service Schedule rates (Schedule 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foreign Service Schedule (22 U.S.C. 3963) pay rates are set forth at Schedule 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreign Service employees must refer to Schedule 2 for their statutory pay rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Veterans Health Administration schedules (Schedule 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: The schedules for the Veterans Health Administration of the Department of Veterans Affairs (38 U.S.C. 7306, 7404; section 301(a) of Public Law 102–40) are set forth at Schedule 3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: VHA-specific pay schedules are attached as Schedule 3 and constitute the authoritative rates for those employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senior Executive Service rates (Schedule 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to section 5382 of title 5, United States Code, the rates of basic pay for senior executives in the Senior Executive Service are set forth on Schedule 4 attached hereto and made a part hereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedule 4 provides the basic pay amounts for SES members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Schedule and specified offices (Schedules 5–7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rates of pay or salaries for Executive Schedule offices, the Vice President and Congress, and Justices and judges are set forth on Schedules 5, 6, and 7 respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically: (a) Executive Schedule (5 U.S.C. 5312–5318) at Schedule 5; (b) Vice President (3 U.S.C. 104) and Congress (2 U.S.C. 31) at Schedule 6; (c) Justices and judges (various statutes) at Schedule 7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniformed services pay and allowances (Schedule 8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rates of monthly basic pay (37 U.S.C. 203(a)), basic allowances for subsistence (37 U.S.C. 402), basic allowances for quarters (37 U.S.C. 403(a)), and cadet/midshipman pay are set forth on Schedule 8.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedule 8 attached to the order contains the specific amounts and constitutes the authoritative pay/allowance rates for uniformed service members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim geographic adjustments — entitlement (Schedule 9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees under statutory pay systems covered under section 1 and members of the United States Park Police assigned to duty stations listed in Schedule 9 shall be entitled, except as provided under subsection (b), to receive an interim geographic adjustment at the rate shown on Schedule 9.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedule 9 lists geographic areas and the interim geographic adjustment rates; entitlement applies to listed employees and duty stations unless a specific exception applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPM regulation of interim geographic adjustments for GS employees
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of Personnel Management shall prescribe regulations governing the application of interim geographic adjustments to General Schedule employees, including the determination of what, if any, geographic adjustments shall be payable in the case of employees receiving special pay rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPM must issue implementing regulations addressing who qualifies and how adjustments interact with special pay rates; these regulations govern application for GS employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretary of State regulation for Foreign Service application
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary of State shall prescribe regulations governing the application of interim geographic adjustments to employees under the Foreign Service Schedule, consistent with OPM regulations and determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State Department regulations must align with OPM's regulations/determinations when applying geographic adjustments to Foreign Service employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretary of Veterans Affairs regulation for VHA employees
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary of Veterans Affairs shall prescribe regulations governing the application of interim geographic adjustments to employees under the schedules for the Veterans Health Administration, consistent with OPM regulations and determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: VHA implementing regulations must be consistent with the OPM-prescribed framework for geographic adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretary of the Interior regulation for U.S. Park Police
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary of the Interior shall prescribe regulations governing the application of interim geographic adjustments to members of the United States Park Police, consistent with OPM regulations and determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interior Department regulations for Park Police geographic adjustments must follow OPM's rules and determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPM authority to extend interim geographic adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of Personnel Management is designated and empowered to exercise the authority of the President under section 302(c)(1)(D) of the Federal Employees Pay Comparability Act of 1990 to extend the application of interim geographic adjustments shown on Schedule 9, upon the request of an agency head, to employees who would not otherwise be covered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPM may, at an agency head's request, extend Schedule 9 adjustments to additional employees not originally covered by the Schedule; this is an exercise of Presidential authority delegated to OPM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective dates for rates and allowances
rubrics_metrics.description: Rates of monthly basic pay and allowances for subsistence and quarters for members of the uniformed services provided for at Schedule 8 are effective on January 1, 1995. The other schedules provided for herein are effective on the first day of the first applicable pay period beginning on or after January 1, 1995.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies distinct effective dates: uniformed services effective Jan 1, 1995; all other attached schedules effective at the start of the first pay period on/after Jan 1, 1995.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supersession of prior Executive Orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Executive Order No. 12826 of December 30, 1992, and Executive Order No. 12886 of December 23, 1993, are superseded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This order replaces and nullifies the listed prior Executive Orders to the extent they conflict with this order.
